newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador's coffee 96-97 crop swings into action.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador's coffee 96-97 crop swings into action.

text.p: Thousands of Salvadorans started cropping the 1996-1997 coffee harvest Wednesday, with expectations for a slight dip in the output this cycle, a top coffee official said Wednesday.
"We have started cutting coffee," Ruben Pineda, the executive director of the Salvadorean Coffee Council, told Reuters.
Pineda said expectations were for the Central American nation to produce around 2.9 million 46-kg bags, down from the 3.1 million bags produced in the 1995-1996 cycle.
But he rejected recent estimates from the Salvadorean Coffee Association winds and rains at the start of the year will cut output to 2.3 million bags, known locally as quintals.
Pineda said output would not be affected to that extent. Rains this week had not damaged crops, he added.
